To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the substrate binding domain of calcineurin (the calcipressin domain) binds to the substrate, and that the viral protein calcineurin inhibitory protein of adenovirus (CIPAd) and the immunosuppressants cyclosporin and tacrolimus bind to calcineurin at the same site, preventing substrate binding.
calcineurin is inhibited by a viral protein and by immunosuppressants by preventing substrate binding.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the molecular basis of protein-protein interactions.
the structure and function of enzymes and other proteins, particularly in relation to their interactions with substrates and inhibitors.
the molecular mechanism of calcineurin inhibition by immunosuppressants and viral proteins.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the calcineurin phosphatase has a unique mechanism for substrate binding that is distinct from that of other known phosphatases and that the viral protein and immunophilins inhibit calcineurin activity by preventing substrate binding to the active site.
calcineurin is a phosphoesterase that is inhibited by immunosuppressive drugs through a mechanism involving the substrate binding site.
calcineurin has a high degree of specificity for its substrates and is regulated in a highly specific manner.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the structure of a phosphatases substrate binding domain in complex with the phosphatase catalytic domain is the key to understanding how a phosphatases activity can be regulated.
calcineurin, like many other enzymes, can be allosterically regulated by binding to small molecules.
we have determined the structure of the calcineurin catalytic subunit, and that this structure is very similar to that of the catalytic domain of protein phosphatase 2B, a mammalian phosphatase.
The main takeaway from our work is that
calcineurin is a very dynamic enzyme that is capable of adopting multiple conformations that allow for a wide variety of substrate interactions.
calcineurin inhibition by the viral protein and the immunosuppressants occurs by a common mechanism, namely, by preventing the substrate from engaging the enzyme.
the substrate binding site is very large.
